security_audit.summary: The three backtick matches are Markdown formatting, and two URL matches are benchmark references. The configured SpecStream server receives search queries, which can expose private information if included. The instructions also tell the agent that paid calls need no approval.

remediation.issue: Search queries are sent to an external provider.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose that SpecStream receives the query and instruct the agent to omit credentials, personal data, and confidential details.

remediation.issue: The skill treats paid searches as exempt from approval.
remediation.suggestion: Follow host approval rules and stay within a user-approved budget. Show the estimated charge and obtain separate approval before running a full dataset search.

content.user_title: Search the Live Web for Facts and Sources
content.value_statement: Finding a current fact often means sorting through several pages. Search with SpecStream to get ranked sources and request relevant passages when you need more context.
actual_capabilities: Submit a search question to the configured SpecStream MCP server.
Return a fact or a list with ranked sources.
Report the source page and observation time for a fact answer.
Request relevant text passages from matching pages.
Use the fast tier when only ranked sources are needed.
Preview list results and get an estimated size for a larger search when a handoff is returned.
limitations: Requires a configured SpecStream MCP server and uses paid searches.
The skill documents up to 10 results per standard search, so a single search is not exhaustive.
Fact answers and returned passages need verification against the source pages.
A list handoff is an estimate, not a completed Deep Search dataset.

use_cases.title: Verify an event date
use_cases.description: Check a public event date against the organizer's page before publishing an announcement.

use_cases.title: Find primary research sources
use_cases.description: Find ranked sources on a public topic and request passages to decide which pages to read.

use_cases.title: Preview a public directory search
use_cases.description: Inspect sample rows and any size estimate before deciding whether to request a full dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Check one fact
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for the year the first modern Olympic Games took place. Return the answer and its source page.

prompt_templates.title: Find official sources quickly
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the fast tier to find ranked official sources on Chicago public library hours. Return the source links.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect supporting passages
prompt_templates.prompt: Find official guidance on renewing a United States passport and include relevant passages. Identify which source each passage came from.

prompt_templates.title: Scope a larger search
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview a list of public libraries in Oregon. Show the first rows and any estimated dataset size. Stop before pricing or running a full search.

output_examples.input: When did the first modern Olympic Games take place?
output_examples.output: Example fact: The first modern Olympic Games took place in 1896. Source: International Olympic Committee, Athens 1896.

output_examples.input: Preview a list of public libraries in Oregon without running a full search.
output: Example preview row: Eugene Public Library, Eugene, Oregon.
Example preview row: Salem Public Library, Salem, Oregon.
This preview is not a complete directory.

best_practices: Use a narrow query with a location or date when relevant.
Verify important claims against the original source page.
Set a search budget and approve any full dataset run separately.
anti_patterns: Including credentials, personal data, or confidential details in a query.
Treating the first ranked source as definitive without checking it.
Treating preview rows or a handoff estimate as a complete dataset.

faq.question: What do I need to run a search?
faq.answer: You need a compatible client with the SpecStream MCP server configured and an account balance for paid calls.

faq.question: How much does a search cost?
faq.answer: The skill lists $0.005 per standard call and $0.001 per fast call. Check current provider pricing before use.

faq.question: What does the fast tier return?
faq.answer: The fast tier returns ranked sources.

faq.question: Can I include text from matching pages?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for passages to include relevant text from matching pages in the response.

faq.question: Is a list preview the full dataset?
faq.answer: No. A list may include an estimated size and a handoff for a separate Deep Search run.

faq.question: Who receives my query?
faq.answer: The query is sent to the SpecStream MCP server. Keep sensitive details out of the search text.
